amata.p: [Na+mata(mara+ta)] (ti) CL=9 Ambata -Sk. The Dhān-Sya Thit states that in Nānatthakosa, the word Amata in neuter gender is in the sense of remnant of sacrifice, ambrosia, water, butter, wealth got with asking for and Nibbāna. In masculine gender, it is in the senses of deity, Dhanvantarī medic. In the feminine gender, it is in the senses of cardamon, long pepper, myrobalam, moonseed vine, gooseberry. It states in its footnote of Dhān-ṭī,25 that the same meanings. Moreover, in Kotthubha, it is in the senses of (Abyayībhāva) 1. deathless, (2) immortal, (3) free from perishing, everlasting; he; thing. (Masc.) (1) deva. (2) the medic deity named Dhanvantarī who cures the deities. (Neut.) (1) not death, (2) Mokkha abode. (3) Sagga abode. (4) ambrosia. (5) liquid flowed from Soma tree. (6) one who kills the poisonous tree. (7) remnant of sacrifice. (8) food obtained without asking. (9) water. (10) alcohol made by cooking and distilling sugar and brown slab-sugar together, sweet alcohol. (11) butter. (12) cow-milk. (13) edible food. (14) rice. (15) sentient being, thing which is adorable, desirable. (16) gold. (17) mercury. (18) poison. (19) Brahmā, in Vācappati, 40 meanings are mentioned.] (Neut.) (1) the Dhamma that has no death- is the cause of no death. Amata Dhamma, Nibbāna. (b) the Dhamma which does not have Uppāda, Ṭhī, Bhaṅga, Nibbāna. (2) the Dhamma which is the cause of attaining Nibbāna, which sends (one) to Nibbāna. (a) Paṭipatti, Paṭipatti which is the casue of reaching Nibbāna. (b) the Dhamma such as Satipaṭṭhāna; One of the 38 Kammaṭṭhānas. (c) Pīti Pāmojja. (d) Kāyagatāsati. (3) Amatasudha, ambrosia. (4) medicine, natural medicine. (b) antidote for defilements. (c) antidote for Dukkha. (5) (a) amata pure water. (b) pure water of Dhamma. (c) Amata juice of Dhamma which is the cause of attaining Magga and Phala. (Fem.) myrobalam. (7) moonseed vine. (Ti) (1) (a) being the cause of deathlessness, The Dhamma, Amatadhamma, Nibbāna. See also Amatogadha. See original. Amata (Ti) [na+mata= (mana+ta)] (a) unknown. (b) known. See (a)(b) amataaggatta, amatagga (2) and anamatagga.
pn: Amata. The Lake of Immortality, in searching for which Bhaddasāla met the Buddha Nārada. Bv-a.154.

C: amata：a. n. [a-mata，Sk. amṛta] 不死的，不死，甘露，涅槃. -gāmin 引導至不死（境界）. -dundubhi 不死之鼓，甘露之鼓. -dasa 見（領會）不死（境界）的人. -dvāra 通往不死之門. -patta 已達（到）不死（境界）的. -pada 不死句，涅槃之境. -phala 不死涅槃之果.

N: amata：（Sanskrit amṛta； Pāḷi root mar to die； = Gr. ambrosia）：＇Deathlessness＇ according to popular belief also the gods＇ drink conferring immortality，is a name for Nibbāna （s. Nibbāna），the final liberation from the wheel of rebirths，and therefore also from the ever-repeated deaths .
P: Amata，<sup>2</sup> （adj.） [see amata<sup>1</sup>] belonging to Amṛta = ambrosial Sn.452 = S.I，189 （amatā vācā = amata-sadisā sādubhāvena SnA 399：“ambrosial”），960 （gacchato amataṁ disaṁ = nibbānaṁ，taṁ hi amatan ti tathā niddisitabbato disā cā ti SnA 572）. Perhaps also at It.46 = 62 （amataṁ dhātuṁ = ambrosial state or Amṛta as dhātu）. （Page 73）

Amata，1 （nt.） [a + mata = mṛta pp. of mṛ，Vedic amṛta = Gr. a]--m（b）rot-o & a]mbrosi/a = Lat. im-mort-a（lis） 1. The drink of the gods，ambrosia，water of immortality，（cp. BSk. amṛta-varṣa “rain of Ambrosia” Jtm 221）. -- 2. A general conception of a state of durability & non-change，a state of security i. e. where there is not any more rebirth or re-death. So Bdhgh at KhA 180 （on Sn.225） “na jāyati na jīyati na mīyati ti amatan ti vuccati”，or at DhA.I，228 “ajātattā na jiyyati na miyyati tasmā amatan ti vuccati”. -- Vin.I，7 = M.I，169 （apārutā tesaṁ amatassa dvārā）； Vin.I，39； D.II，39，217，241； S.I，32 （= rāgadosamoha-khayo），193； III，2 （°ena abhisitta “sprinkled with A.”）； IV，94 （°assa dātā），370； V，402 （°assa patti）； A.I，45 sq.； III，451； IV，455； V，226 sq.，256 sq. （°assa dātā）； J.I，4 （V.25）； IV，378，386； V，456 （°mahā-nibbāna）； Sn.204，225，228 （= nibbāna KhA 185）； Th.1，310 （= agada antidote）； It.46 = 62 （as dhātu），80 （°assa dvāra）； Dh.114，374 （= amata-mahā-nibbāna DhA.IV，110）； Miln.258 （°dhura savanûpaga），319 （agado amataṁ & nibbānaṁ amataṁ），336 （amatena lokaṁ abhisiñci Bhagavā），346 （dhamm’âmataṁ）； DA.I，217 （°nibbāna）； DhA.I，87 （°ṁ pāyeti）； Dāvs II.34； V，31； Sdhp.1，209，530，571.

--ogadha diving into the ambrosia （of Nibbāna） S.V，41，54，181，220，232； A.III，79，304； IV，46 sq.，317，387； V，105 sq.； Sn.635； Th.1，179，748； Dh.411 （= amataṁ nibbānaṁ ogahetvā DhA.IV，186）； Vv 5020. --osadha the medicine of Ambrosia，ambrosial medicine Miln.247. --gāmin going or leading to the ambrosia （of Nibbāna） S.I，123； IV，370； V，8； A.III，329； Th.2，222. --dasa one who sees Amata or Nibbāna Th.1，336. --dundubhi the drum of the Immortal （Nibbāna） M.I，171 = Vin.I，8 （has °dudrabhi）. --dvāra the door to Nibbāna M.I，353； S.I，137 = Vin.I，5； S.II，43，45，58，80； A.V，346. --dhātu the element of Ambrosia or Nibbāna A.III，356. --patta having attained to Ambrosia A.IV，455. --pada the region or place of Ambrosia S.I，212 （“Bourne Ambrosial” trsln. p. 274）； II，280； Dh.21 （= amatassa adhigama-vupāyo vuttaṁ hoti DhA.I，228）. --phala ambrosial fruit S.I，173 = Sn.80. --magga the path to Ambrosia DhA.I，94. （Page 73）
